passage:
"Sir, you want me to hold the register?" Jahnavi asked, hovering by the staff-room door.
"Thank you, Jahnavi." Rafiq Sir rubbed his eyes.
"You look tired today."
"A little. My mother is unwell, and I slept badly. Nothing you need to worry about."
Jahnavi nodded. In class she did not fidget or talk, and when the chalk box fell she picked up the pieces before anyone laughed. At the bell she stacked the notebooks neatly on his desk.
"Jahnavi," he said, "that helped more than you know."
She smiled. "I hope your mother feels better, Sir."

qa.q: What did Rafiq Sir say was wrong when Jahnavi told him he looked tired?
qa.a: He said his mother was unwell and he had slept badly.

qa.q: What made Jahnavi behave calmly and kindly in class that day?
qa.a: She noticed her teacher looked tired and worried and understood he was a person with troubles, so she chose to be quiet and helpful.

qa.q: What else could Jahnavi do on a day her teacher looks stressed?
qa.a: She could help carry books, keep her voice low and be patient, without prying into what is wrong.

qa.q: How might Rafiq Sir have felt when Jahnavi stacked the notebooks?
qa.a: He probably felt touched and a little less alone, which is why he said her help mattered more than she knew. 🙂

grounding: A child notices a tired, worried teacher, sees him as a person and offers small helpful acts.

passage: In Class 4B, Uma Ma'am usually started the day with a joke. Today she didn't. Her eyes were puffy, and twice she looked at her phone and then put it face down. Sahil noticed. When she dropped the pile of notebooks by the door, a few boys snickered. Sahil got up and helped her gather them without saying anything. At recess the others planned to make noise in the next period 'because she won't even notice'. Sahil shook his head. 'She looks really tired. Let's not.' He stayed quiet all through the lesson and put his hand up for an answer when nobody else did. Before home time, Uma Ma'am caught his eye and gave him a small, grateful smile.

qa.q: How many times did Uma Ma'am look at her phone?
What did Sahil feel when he noticed Uma Ma'am's puffy eyes?
qa.a: Concerned and caring; he sensed she was tired and worried, so he wanted to help rather than add to it.

qa.q: What small things did Sahil do that helped?
qa.a: He helped gather the notebooks, talked the others out of making noise, and answered in class.

qa.q: How might Uma Ma'am have felt about Sahil's help?
qa.a: Grateful and less alone on a hard day; she gave him a small smile before home time.

grounding: A boy notices his teacher looks tired and worried, and responds with small acts of kindness in class.

passage:
Monday. Uday Sir, who usually made science fun with his magnet tricks, snapped at the back row and forgot to set homework. Jyoti noticed dark circles under his eyes.
Wednesday. At the gate, Jyoti heard him on the phone: 'I'll come to the hospital straight after school.' His voice was small. In class, when the noise rose, Jyoti whispered to her row, 'Let's be quiet today. I think something's wrong at home for him.' Her row went quiet, then the next one.
Friday. Jyoti handed him a card signed by the whole class: 'Hope your week gets better, Sir.' He read it twice and cleared his throat. 'Thank you. That helps more than you know.' Then he did a magnet trick, a small one.

qa.q: What did Uday Sir usually make science fun with?
What was Jyoti feeling after hearing the phone call?
qa.a: Concerned and sympathetic; his small voice made her realise he was worried about something at home.

qa.q: How did Jyoti turn her noticing into kindness?
qa.a: She asked her row to be quiet and later gave him a card signed by the whole class.

qa.q: How did the card affect Uday Sir?
qa.a: He was touched; he read it twice, cleared his throat and said it helped more than they knew.

grounding: Over a week a girl notices her teacher is worried and tired, and leads her class in small kindnesses.
